content:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's batch-size tweak I’m seeing p99 tail spikes on streaming chat in prod (small traffic). Was trying to unify microbatch=8 across streaming + non-streaming to simplify scheduling.
liam: Ugh, that was the change? Which models/instance type?
maya: gptx-medium on a8x, CPU comp host is the usual. Baseline before change: p50 60ms, p95 140ms, p99 220ms for streaming first-token. After change: p50 70ms, p95 170ms, p99 420ms.
dina: That's consistent with microbatching increasing TTFB for streaming. Streaming benefits from tiny microbatches (1-2) so we can push first-token quickly.
zach: For non-streaming completions, microbatch 8 helped throughput: throughput +22%, token latency amortized better. So it's a tradeoff.
manual note from perf-bot: recent deploy 1741143001 applied default microbatch=8 to unified pool
anika: Kernel selection also matters — at small batch sizes our runtime picks the FlashAttention kernel with lower startup overhead, but when batch>=4 it switches to the fused-kernel that has higher setup but better steady throughput. That switch increases tail for short seq streaming.
liam: Can we pick kernel per-request based on stream_flag + seq_len + estimated latency budget?
dina: Yes. Suggested heuristic:
```
if streaming:
  microbatch = min(2, incoming_concurrency)
  kernel = low_startup_kernel
else:
  microbatch = min(16, incoming_concurrency)
  kernel = high_throughput_kernel
```
But need to watch KV cache behavior — grouping many non-streaming requests into big batches increases KV reuse but also increases mem pressure.
maya: I profiled KV cache hits: with microbatch 8 on non-streaming, cache hit rate went from 62% -> 78% and average token exec time dropped 14%. For streaming microbatch 8, KV hit rate stayed ~65% but latency had high variance.
zach: What about tail-latency analysis? Any traces showing queuing effects vs kernel jitter?
manual trace dump from perf-bot:
```
trace_id: ab12
queue_wait: 180ms
kernel_start: 12ms
kv_lookup: 6ms
token_gen_90p: 40ms
token_gen_99p: 360ms
```
Suggests queuing + worst-case kernel path contributes to p99.
anika: One concrete approach: split pools — low-latency pool (microbatch 1-2, small kernels, reserved capacity) for streaming chat; high-throughput pool (microbatch 8-16, quantized kernels, batching windows=20ms) for non-streaming completions. Use smart-routing: if request.streaming==true -> low-latency-pool; else route to throughput-pool unless customer SLA says low-latency.
liam: We'll need autoscaler rules per pool and per-model kernel profiles in the model catalog. Also add a fallback: if low-latency pool is saturated, fall back to a degraded path that streams with chunked tokens (send first token from low-batch path even if rest is processed in throughput pool).
dina: Quick experiment plan:
- A/B for 2 weeks on small % traffic
- Add per-request kernel trace flags
- Track first-token p50/p95/p99 separately from full-completion p50/p95/p99
- Metrics: KV hit-rate, queue_wait distribution, kernel_type histogram

maya: OK I’ll roll a canary with streaming->microbatch=2, non-streaming->microbatch=12 + kernel hints. Will ping if p99 holds or regresses.
zach: If you want, I can add dynamic microbatching: increase batch size if queue_wait > 30ms to try and recover throughput, but cap that for streaming.
maya: Yes please add a hard cap for streaming. Also add an alert rule: streaming p99 > 300ms -> rollback to previous routing immediately.
perf-bot: action: created issue PERF-4823 "split microbatch pools for streaming vs non-streaming" assigned to maya, liam, due 2024-11-05 :spiral_calendar:
